3.3 Among others, these petitioners as defendants Nos.5-7 and 12-17 entered appearance and contested the suit by way of submitting a joint written statement denying materials allegations made in the plaint and contended therein, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable with the simple prayer for partition and that the suit suffers from defect of parties and hotchpot. It is further contended that long before the suit the disputed properties were partitioned amicably by mets and bounds between the predecessors of the parties by a deed of partition dated 30-6-1939. Shaheb Ullah Pramanik, Mohit Ullah Pramanik and Mohorbi Bewa transferred two- wan (a local land measurement in Bogra) of land out of the suit land in favour of Shahebullah Pramanik, the predecessor of these defendants-appellants-petitioners vide registered sale deed dated 10-2-1925. The said land of two wans measuring 58 decimals were recorded in plot No. 3124 and 4735 in CS Khatian No.889 but CS Khatian No.1477 was erroneously written in the said sale deed out of bonafide mistake. After the said sale deed was registered, Syeedullah Pramanik, Mohitullah Pramanik and Shaharbi Bewa got their title extinguished to the said amount of land. It is further stated that Syed Ali Pramanik, the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties, was the party to the said partition deed dated 30-6-1939 and in view of thereof MRR Khatian was prepared in the name of the parties to the partition deed. As per partition deed, Syed Ali Pramanik acquired 1.28 acres of land in CS Khatian No.1388 (schedule 2 to the plaint) and 1.06 acres of land in CS Khatian No.218 (schedule No.1) totaling 2.34 acres of land and MRR Khatian Nos. 237 and 442 were correctly prepared in his name. After the demise of Syed Ali Pramanik, the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties inherited 2.34 acres of land in the partible holdings and that they have no right, title and interest in any land in CS khatian no 889 (Schedule 3). They are only entitled to 2.34 acres of land. In the above circumstances, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4.2 The learned Counsel adds that the deed was acted upon and the outcome thereof has been subsequently reflected in the preparation and publication of the MRR Khatians prepared in view of the said deed. 

 4.3 Mr. NV. Zahidul Bari also urges that Syed Ullah Pramanik and others, the predecessors of the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties, transferred 58 decimals of land vide registered kabala dated 10-2-1925, exhibit-Uma, to Shaheb Ullah Pramanik, the predecessor of these 'petitioners and accordingly MRR khatian No.1478 has been prepared in the name of these petitioners in respect of the said land but this transfer has been erroneously kept out of consideration. 

 4.7 He also submits that the document dated 2-4-1946 despite containing mistaken plot number was considered for the plaintiffs to give them benefit, whereas the deed of sale dated 10-2-1925 containing mistaken khatian number was not considered in favour of these defendants-appellants-petitioners. Therefore, these petitioners have been discriminated for disregarding the Rule of Parity. 

 5.1 In view of the foregoing rival submissions of the learned Counsels, the first and foremost contention to be resolved in this revision is whether Partition Suit No.92 of 1993 is at all maintainable in the instant form and manner with lone relief of partition, or any additional prayer for declaration of title was required to be sought besides partition. The pleadings of the parties are found to be akin to the submissions of the learned Counsel for the defendants-appellants-petitioners that the CS and SA Khatian did not properly record, the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties. Here the learned Counsel assails the maintainability of the suit on the ground of seeking therein the solitary prayer for partition. In the case of Chinnzoy Chowdhury and others vs Sree Mridul Chowdhury and others [23 BLD (AD) 2003, page-83-87 : 55 DLR (AD) 115], both trial court and the High Court Division held the suit to be maintainable with simple prayer for partition. Some ancestral properties were the subject matter of partition in the suit. But in the appeal before the Hon'ble Appellate Division the question of maintainability had been assailed wherein His Lordship observed as follows— 

 5.2 In our instant case, the entire scenario regarding accrual of the title of plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties to suit land has been narrated in the plaint in broad details. No hurdle seems to be apparent to determine the acquisition of title by plaintiff and hence their names, whether recorded or omitted to be recorded in a particular khatian is quite immaterial, particularly when the laid down principle is that Record-of Rights does not create or extinguish any title to the lands incorporated therein. Be it mentioned, CS Khatian though being a key land record document holding significant evidential value is not conclusive proof of ownership. Thus the contention agitated on the issue of maintainability merits no substance.
